title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier plus a bounded automated repair budget improves the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation versus accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we executed 300 paired intents (100 per difficulty stratum: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and a deterministic semantic validator. Each paired intent produced one shared_initial generation reused for: (a) baseline — accept single shot; (b) guarded — validator + ≤1 automated repair. Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.996667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact two‑sided McNemar p = 1.0; 95% paired bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and repair budget the single‑shot generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue to one sequencing omission corrected by a single constrained repair. We archive preregistration, execution, validator traces, repair transcripts, and analysis artifacts to support reproducibility. Results are interpreted with respect to estimand conditioning (shared_initial), validator coverage, repair budget, and operational deployment policies.

sections.introduction: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to translate operator intent into device configurations and to propose network‑change workflows. For pre‑deployment changes the operationally relevant properties are semantic (sequencing, reachability, policy preservation) rather than merely syntactic. A common mitigation pattern is generate→validate→repair: pair a generative model with a deterministic validator and allow constrained automated edits. Prior work shows that tool augmentation can improve surface correctness, but published results often conflate benefits from multiple independent model draws with benefits that arise deterministically from post‑generation checking. To isolate the latter, we preregistered a paired experiment that conditions on a single LLM draw per intent (the shared_initial estimand) and compares accepting that candidate verbatim versus running a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair. Our contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under a single shared LLM draw; (2) a complete archived execution and analysis bundle including validator traces and the single automated repair transcript; (3) an evidence‑grounded interpretation of ceiling effects, estimand conditioning, and operational implications for NetOps pipelines.
sections.related_work: Recent surveys and system papers document active application of LLMs to intent→configuration translation, configuration synthesis, protocol test generation, and repair in NetOps [1–4]. Tool‑augmented frameworks (planner‑centric, ReAct, tool‑use agents) enable LLMs to call external validators and simulators for multi‑step workflows and have been proposed to improve correctness and coordination [5,6]. Empirical reports indicate that deterministic checks and generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve correctness metrics relative to unconstrained generation, but reported gains depend strongly on validator expressiveness, task distribution, and whether pipelines permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration [3,7]. Works on hallucination detection and deterministic safety nets further emphasize that detector/validator coverage and the allowed repair operator set are primary determinants of guarded pipeline value [8]. Our study is positioned to measure only the bounded, post‑hoc deterministic rescue available when policy constrains model calls.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. The design was preregistered (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) before the main run; the primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) on N = 300 paired intents under pre‑specified inclusion/exclusion rules. Task generation and strata. A deterministic task generator produced a synthetic topology suite stratified into low/medium/high difficulty (100 pairs per stratum). Each task encodes intent, initial/final device states, sequencing invariants (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), protected interfaces, and required command sequences. Shared_initial protocol and model configuration. To bound analysis to deterministic rescue, each pair produced exactly one shared_initial candidate using gpt-5-mini; that identical candidate was evaluated under both conditions (no resampling). Validator and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used a deterministic netops validator implementing full intent constraint checks (sequencing, required commands, preservation of unspecified state, topology invariants). The guarded condition allowed at most one automated, localized repair edit (sequencing insertions or similarly constrained fixes); repaired candidates were deterministically re‑validated. Contamination controls, missingness, and stopping rules. The preregistration included negative controls, contamination detection, and a stopping rule halting the run if >20% of attempted pairs were excluded due to dual‑call outages. Analysis executor and inferential plan. The confirmatory analysis used a paired binary executor producing contingency counts (n11,n10,n01,n00), an exact two‑sided McNemar test, and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000). Sensitivity analyses and exploratory stratum tests were planned and archived.
sections.results: Execution integrity. The registered adapter completed the confirmatory run: completed_episode_count = 600, complete_pair_count = 300. Model call accounting: model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair invocation). No provider outages or excluded pairs occurred; deterministic reconciliation checks passed. Primary outcomes. Binary scoring yielded baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667; guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). Contingency counts: n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact two‑sided McNemar on discordant counts (n10,n01) returned p = 1.0. Absolute paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000) = [0.00, 0.01]. Stratum diagnostics. Per‑stratum tallies: low baseline = 100/100, guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100, guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100, guarded = 100/100. The single discordant case lies in the high stratum. Repair diagnostic. The solitary discordant episode invoked the permitted automated repair: the validator flagged a sequencing omission (missing required admin down before VLAN/MTU change); the constrained single edit inserted the missing sequencing command and the validator then reported valid == true. Thus the guarded pipeline deterministically rescued one sequencing omission with one permitted repair call. Cost and operational footprint. The guarded pipeline required one extra repair stage call across 300 pairs, indicating minimal additional model‑call cost under the chosen repair budget and edit operator. Statistical interpretation. The near‑ceiling baseline (299/300) produced minimal discordance (m = 1), limiting the sensitivity of the exact test to detect small absolute differences. The bootstrap CI bounds plausible absolute paired improvements to ≤1 percentage point under the shared_initial estimand and the supplied synthetic suite.
sections.discussion: Estimand alignment and operational meaning. The shared_initial estimand maps to operational policies that limit model calls; it measures deterministic rescue applied to the same LLM output and excludes benefits attainable by resampling or interactive verifier‑guided regeneration. If a deployment permits multiple model draws, evaluations should adopt a different estimand. Ceiling effects and pilot omission. The preregistration planned an optional pilot to estimate discordance and calibrate power; that pilot was not executed. Consequently, baseline performance reached near ceiling on the chosen synthetic suite and observable deterministic rescue was rare. Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The single failure observed was sequencing omission; other failure classes (reachability, ACL removal) were not encountered at scale in this suite. The guarded pipeline’s marginal utility therefore depends on (i) the deployed failure‑mode distribution and (ii) validator expressiveness. Repair budget tradeoffs. We intentionally constrained automated repair to a single, localized edit to bound deterministic rescue; iterative repairs, broader edit operators, or verifier‑guided regeneration would constitute a different estimand and are expected to increase rescue opportunities but also model‑call cost. Operational implications for NetOps CI/CD. For policies that tightly constrain model calls, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful bound on deterministic verifier/repair rescue. Under the supplied conditions, bounded repair yielded a deterministic rescue at negligible extra model cost, but absolute gains are small when baseline single‑shot quality is near 100%.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, archived paired study (N = 300 pairs) conditioning on a single LLM draw per intent, adding a deterministic validator plus at most one constrained automated repair increased unflagged verifier passes from 299/300 to 300/300 (absolute paired difference = 0.00333; McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00,0.01]). The guarded pipeline deterministically rescued one sequencing omission via a single permitted repair. These results are specific to the shared_initial estimand, the synthetic task distribution, the declared generator (gpt-5-mini), the validator semantics, and the repair budget. We release full preregistration, execution logs, validator traces, repair transcripts, and analysis artifacts to enable targeted follow‑up studies that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distributions, and repair budgets.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were generated deterministically; real‑world heterogeneity may expose different failure modes and increase validator marginal utility.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and the declared deterministic validator were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or richer/diverse validators.
Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance approached 100% (299/300) on this suite, producing minimal discordance and reduced power to detect small absolute improvements.
Pilot not executed: the preregistered optional pilot for discordance estimation was not run, so no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed.
Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions on a single LLM draw and therefore omits verifier benefits achievable via resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration.
Repair budget: the guarded condition permitted at most one automated repair per pair; broader or iterative repair strategies could yield different outcomes.
